fs.read: September CPI beat on both headline and core, and the trend is accelerating.
ev: Headline CPI 3.7% y/y vs 3.6% expected; +0.6% m/m vs 0.4% in August.
Core CPI 2.6% y/y vs 2.5% expected (prior 2.4%); core +0.3% m/m vs 0.2% expected.
Gasoline rose 9.1% in the month and made up about half of the headline gain.
ct: Core at 2.6% is still moderate next to headline; energy drove most of the monthly rise.
Energy-led inflation can fade quickly if oil retreats.

fs.read: Payrolls are weak but layoffs are low, so the labor picture is mixed.
ev: September payrolls +29k vs a 45k 12-month average; unemployment 4.2%; wages +0.1% m/m.
Initial jobless claims 194k vs 200k expected (week ending Oct 17); continuing claims 1.728M.
ct: Low claims say layoffs are not rising, which supports further Fed tightening (bearish).
Weak hiring lowers hike odds and signals slowing growth. Net: mixed.

fs.read: Fed is mid hiking cycle; the hold on Wednesday is priced, so December guidance is the risk.
ev: Sept 16: 25bp hike to 3.75–4.00%; minutes showed unanimous support.
CME FedWatch: about 91% hold on Oct 28 (hike about 9%), and about 78–84% for a December hike; futures imply roughly 2.7 hikes over 12 months.
Reuters poll: 94 of 100 economists expect a hold; all 100 expect a December hike.
Decision Wed Oct 28, 2:00 PM ET, then Chair Warsh's press conference; core PCE is due Thursday.
ct: A hold is almost fully priced, so the decision itself is unlikely to move markets.
If Warsh leaves December open, hike pricing could unwind and relieve equities.

fs.read: Nominal and real yields are both high, a hostile level for long-duration tech.
ev: Fri close: 2y 4.686%, 10y 5.001%, 30y 5.329%; 10y is about +81bp year to date.
10-year TIPS real yield about 2.38% (Bloomberg, Oct 23).
Thursday's 17bp drop was a flight to safety during the AI selloff and was partly reversed Friday.
ct: Yields fell from 5.13% on Wednesday and are about 20bp below a month ago.
Nasdaq 100 finished Friday flat despite higher yields, so some pressure may be priced in.
Real yield came from one quote source and was not cross-checked.

fs.read: Brent is near $117 and the Iran war is spreading to Gulf states.
ev: Brent $116.72 on Sunday vs $113.90 Friday; WTI above $100 Friday.
Houthi missiles were intercepted over Riyadh Sunday and Washington is pulling diplomatic families out of Saudi Arabia.
US crude stocks are down 79M barrels since the war began on Feb 28.
ct: De-escalation or talks headlines have repeatedly reversed oil spikes.
Weekend headlines are unconfirmed until official statements follow.

fs.read: Activity is booming, which helps earnings but keeps the Fed hawkish.
ev: Flash composite PMI 57.6 (prior 58.4); manufacturing 56.0, a 53-month high; services 57.9.
New orders at a 4.5-year high; selling prices rose at the fastest rate since Aug 2022.
Initial jobless claims 194k, below the 200k consensus.
ct: Strong demand plus price pressure supports more hikes, which hurts valuations (why NQ is 0, not positive).
Services slipped and output expectations cooled from September.

fs.read: The dollar is mid-range and not driving the move.
ev: DXY about 101.8 on Oct 23, inside a one-month range of 100.87 to 102.94.
ct: A break above 103 would tighten financial conditions; nothing suggests that yet.

fs.read: AI-spending doubts are hitting the group that leads NQ.
ev: Nasdaq Composite fell 2.6% on Thursday on AI-spending worries, its largest drop since June.
Credit default swap spreads widened on a host of AI companies; tech bond yields rose.
Mega-cap earnings and the Fed land in the same week.
ct: Nasdaq 100 finished Friday flat, so selling momentum may be fading.
Strong mega-cap results could reverse the AI-capex narrative quickly.

fs.read: Nasdaq options are pricing elevated risk; the S&P is calmer.
ev: VIX 19.45 on Oct 23, up from 16.68 on Oct 21 (52-week range 13.38–35.30).
QQQ implied volatility 26.3% (elevated) vs SPY 15.5% (normal).
Credit default swap spreads widened on AI companies.
ct: VIX under 20 is not a stress level.
Only AI-linked credit was checked; broad credit spreads were not.

gaps: Real yield taken from one quote source; hike odds differ slightly by source (CME ~9% vs prediction markets ~6%).
Monday pre-market not yet observed; refresh around 9:00 ET.
docs.sum: Five of nine factors lean bearish: hot CPI, a Fed hold that comes with a likely December hike, 5% nominal and 2.4% real yields, Brent near $117 on Gulf escalation, and AI-spending doubts. Strong PMIs and low claims keep growth from being a drag, and jobs and the dollar are neutral. NQ scores about -0.83 and ES about -0.65, so ES is nearer the Medium cutoff. Event risk is high this week.
docs.title: 9:30 open overview, Mon Oct 26 (preliminary, built Sunday)
flip: Warsh leaves a December hike open or sounds patient, unwinding hike pricing.
Brent falls sharply on a credible Iran de-escalation.
Core PCE (Thu) prints below the ~3.1% nowcast and mega-cap earnings reverse the AI-capex fear.
docs.risk: High (FOMC Wed 2 PM with Chair Warsh, core PCE Thu, mega-cap earnings, Iran escalation, 5% 10y)
